name: Maeng Itneg
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible
sweep_summary: Maeng Itneg (maen1235) is not in the catalog. All three title-keyword items in this search of works with stress in the title record are noise: Sanz 2017 (English -ory stress), Archibald 1997 (L2 English stress; Crossref record confirmed, De Gruyter landing 405), Schweitzer et al. 2010 (German-corpus pitch accent phonetics; sister Interspeech abstract seen). They were attached to this language only because 'storage' also appears in McCord's 2009 Maeng-values thesis title. lsphil.net has no 2019 programme; archive.org has nothing. High priority to acquire (likely the best statement; contact UP Diliman Linguistics / LSP). The only first-hand Maeng data held by the project, Walton's 2003 SIL wordlists (re-inspected by eye), mark stress with a tick on both penultimate and final syllables and state no rule, so the best new statement = not found.

earlier_scan.source_named: SIL resource search blocked (not reachable by automated download); only Himes 1997 comparative reference named; no Maeng Itneg description located.

sources.citation: Arndt-Lappe, Sabine and Ernestus, Mirjam (2020). Morpho-phonological alternations: The role of lexical storage. In Word knowledge and word usage. A cross-disciplinary guide to the mental lexicon. De Gruyter Mouton. pp. 191-227.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The chapter is a psycholinguistic survey of lexical storage vs. computation for morphologically complex words; its stress content is entirely about English (stress preservation in derived words, variable secondary stress, noun-noun compound stress), with further data from Spanish, Dutch and German. a full-text search for stress/accent Itneg/Tinguian/Maeng/Ma-eng/Philippin over the chapter = 0 hits; no Cordilleran or Philippine language is described anywhere in it (Tagalog appears only in the title of the Zuraw 2010 reference). It is in the Glottolog list for maen1235 only through the keyword…

sources.citation: Walton, Charles (compiler). 2003 [data 1/25/03]. Maeng Itneg, Laplapog, Villaviciosa Wordlist (1966 Expanded Philippine Word List, 372 items; resource person Jose Lagen Sr.). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 77368, unpublished handwritten draft, 10 pp. [NOT in this search of works with stress in the title's item list — held by the project from the prior check]
sources.quote: [handwritten forms, stress tick transcribed as ' before the stressed syllable] 3. all am'?in; 7. anus 'obit; 9. ashamed maba'?in; 10. ashes 'dapo; 20. bird 'ayam; 25. blind 'kuwap; 26. blood 'dara; 27. to blow (as a fire) sap'?oy; 34. breast 'susu; 40. call pu'kaw
sources.note: Raw data only, no prose rule. A raised tick precedes the stressed syllable. Inspected page 1 (p.2): tick before the penult in 'obit 'anus', 'kuwap 'blind', 'dara 'blood', 'ayam 'bird', 'susu 'breast', 'dapo 'ashes'; tick before the final syllable in am'?in 'all', maba'?in 'ashamed', pu'kaw 'call', sap'?oy 'to blow'. Both penultimate and final stress occur, i.e. stress is not fixed and looks lexically contrastive as elsewhere in Cordilleran, but no statement of a rule is made.

sources.note: Nothing on phonology. 18,000 speakers (2003 SIL); no dialects known; lexical similarity Tubo 60% Ilocano/68% Northern Kankanaey, Villaviciosa 76% Ilocano/61% N. Kankanaey.

sources.citation: Walton, Charles (compiler). 2003. Maeng Itneg, Laplapog, Villavisciosa Wordlist. 1966 Expanded Philippine Word List, 372 items, resource person Jose Lagen Sr. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 77368 (unpublished draft, CC BY-NC-SA), 10 pp. handwritten.
sources.note: Data only, no prose. A raised tick before the stressed syllable marks stress on either the penult ('obit 'anus', 'kuwap 'blind', 'dara 'blood', 'ayam 'bird', 'banka 'boat', 'aso 'dog', 'ina 'ear') or the final syllable (ma'nok 'chicken', nu'an 'carabao', ti'mid 'chin', bi'lag 'to dry', ta'pok 'dust', maba'?in 'ashamed'). No rule stated; placement is evidently lexical/contrastive.

sources.citation: Walton, Charles (compiler). 2003. Maeng Itneg, Tubo Wordlist. 1966 Expanded Philippine Word List, 372 items, resource person Francisco Cayasen, Tubo. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 77375 (unpublished draft, CC BY-NC-SA), 10 pp. handwritten.
sources.note: Data only. Same tick convention; stress on penult ('awak 'body', 'kuwap 'blind', 'lasap 'burn a field', 'gatang 'buy') and on final (am'?in 'all', ba'?in 'ashamed', ni'tit 'black'). Marginal note 'all b initial is [bw]'. No rule stated.
